Implemented truncate(s, n) function that:
1. Returns s unchanged if len(s) <= n
2. If len(s) < n + 3 (string only slightly longer than n), returns s[:n] + '...'
3. Otherwise returns s[:n-3] + '...' so total length is exactly n
This handles the edge case where the string is only 1-2 characters longer

Implemented truncate(s, n) in src/truncate.py. The function returns s unchanged if len(s) <= n. Otherwise, it attempts to truncate at the last word boundary (space) within the first n characters, appending '...'. If no word boundary exists, it takes the first n characters and appends '...'.
